# phi-scan: synthetic
#
# Page excerpts in the shape pypdf produces for the three ACIP/ files. Those
# are not guideline documents at all, they are browser print-to-PDF captures of
# CDC schedule pages, and the header they carry is what says so: a print
# timestamp, the page title, the source URL and an "n of m" folio.
#
# pypdf folds the title in after the timestamp and the folio in after the URL,
# so the capture contributes exactly one page-repeated line -- the stamp and
# title together. This fixture used to put the stamp on a line of its own, which
# is what fitz does and what no real file here does, and the classifier passed
# against it while finding zero captures in the corpus. The shape is the test.
#
# The timestamp is date-shaped, which is why this file declares the pragma above.
# It is a browser artifact from a public CDC page and no patient is anywhere near
# it, but the shape layer cannot know that and should not have to.
#
# Four pages, form-feed separated, header lines stripped by the loader. CDC
# content is federal and public domain, so unlike the AHA excerpts this one could
# have been copied verbatim; the body is still trimmed to what the tests need.
Recommended Vaccinations for Adults
For Everyone
JULY 2, 2025
 An official website of the United States government
Here's how you know
